title: No, "AI" will never become conscious — A Lovely Harmless Monster
excerpt: In the late 20th century, there was a gorilla named Koko who made waves by displaying an apparent ability to talk to humans in sign language. This would've had shocking implications for life as we know it, but the science determined that what she was doing wasn't actually "using language". Through reinforcement learning, she had come to realize that mimicking the hand signals of her human handlers would result in certain outcomes. She knew that making the hand signal for "food" might convince the humans to give her food, but she didn't have the brain structures that would allow her to understand that the hand sign represented food in an abstract way. She could learn word associations, but she couldn't understand the grammar and syntax required for the communication to actually be a "language". We did not discover Gorilla sapiens.
content_html:
In the late 20th century, there was a gorilla named Koko who made waves by displaying an apparent ability to talk to humans in sign language. This would've had shocking implications for life as we know it, but the science determined that what she was doing wasn't actually "using language". Through reinforcement learning, she had come to realize that mimicking the hand signals of her human handlers would result in certain outcomes. She knew that making the hand signal for "food" might convince the humans to give her food, but she didn't have the brain structures that would allow her to understand that the hand sign represented food in an abstract way. She could learn word associations, but she couldn't understand the grammar and syntax required for the communication to actually be a "language". We did not discover Gorilla sapiens.

That's not to say it's impossible; whatever mutation made human brains develop language could happen again, and if it does, we should take it seriously. I don't think this will happen the way it appeared with Koko; we'll probably notice an animal communicating in a slightly more complex way, but it might take eons before the communication becomes something we recognize as language. Or we'll discover a heretofore unknown species of animal that has already undergone this transformation. Extremely unlikely, but it could happen.

So what about the opposite? If a conscious animal can't spontaneously learn to use language, can a language-using being develop consciousness? Some people think it's possible; some claim to believe it's already happened, that currently-existing LLMs are already conscious. This is a possibility I'm more skeptical about.

First off, I dispute the idea that LLMs are "using language" at all. They're doing something that looks, to a casual observer, a lot like using language; but lest we forget, so did Koko. The way LLMs learned language is basically a high-speed, highly specialized version of the way Koko "learned" a "language". We made a computer program simulate an animal that "wants things", then taught it to mimic human language in a way that "gets it what it wants". If you had a virtual Koko whose brain was the same but worked a trillion times faster, she might also be able to "learn language" to a similar degree.

Ted Chiang wrote the definitive debunking of AI consciousness, so I won't rehash his analysis, go read it. (if the full article won't load, try disabling javascript.) But I think continuing the animal comparison will illuminate why "AI consciousness" is not only impossible, but a concept that only makes sense in a religious framework.

We don't know exactly when or how consciousness first appeared, but we do know why, because the "why" of evolution is always the same: consciousness evolved because it helped an animal survive. Some organism mutated some feature resembling a prototypical brain [edit: this isn't entirely correct, see this comment from TNSBWM] with some primordial spark of awareness; this (somehow) helped it survive and reproduce in greater numbers than the purely stimulus-based animals around them. Over millions of years, the organism kept outcompeting the ones in the niche without this mutation, and as they kept reproducing, the mutation kept mutating. Brains got bigger and the spark grew along with them.

This is how evolution works in the natural world: (mutations + suitability)*(time) = [differences]. The most useful differences within a particular niche become the dominant ones.

Evolution is a useful metaphor for machine learning, because some concepts from evolution map neatly onto self-improvement algorithms. However, this metaphor has become load-bearing for the AI industry, whose existence depends on making sure we confuse the map for the territory forever. If self-improvement algorithms are sort of like evolution, and computers can "evolve" a zillion times faster than organic life, then AI will probably "evolve" into SUPER AI within the next 5 years, or if not, then definitely the next 10, trust me bro.

The problem is that a metaphor is only a metaphor. In reality, machine learning is different from evolution in important ways.

Have you ever played with the Genetic Algorithm 2D Car Thingy? If not, check it out, it's a fun little toy. Amorphous masses of circles and polygons appear on the left. The circles rotate clockwise. If a circle touches the ground, it will propel the mass of polygons it's attached to forward, until gravity and the shape of the terrain forces it to stop.

In round 1, most of the masses don't get very far. Maybe one or two will get lucky and be generated with two wheels touching the ground. These will go the farthest, but still quickly fall over because their shape is random, not optimized for traversing the hills and valleys in front of them.

Once all the "cars" stop, the universe resets. A new batch of "cars" is generated, using traits from the most successful "cars" in round 1. In this round, the cars that went the furthest reappear with new mutations, and if the mutations make them more car-like, they'll do a little better. This process repeats, and after a few generations, the masses start to resemble cars.

Their wheels get more oriented towards the ground; their bodies become longer and sleeker; their weird random appendages shrink and flatten out. Meaningless bundles of shapes were given the same goal we have: to survive as long as possible. And, thanks to a computer simulation, we can watch them evolve to achieve that goal. It's super cool!

Here's a question you might ask: the cars would be able to survive longer if the gravity wasn't so strong, right? But the simulation is stuck at Earth gravity (9.8 m/s) unless the human operator decides to intervene. So why don't the cars learn how to hack the simulation and turn the gravity down? Wouldn't that be a huge evolutionary advantage?

Well no, you probably wouldn't ask that question, because it's very silly. Obviously the cars aren't literally evolving: it's a metaphor. It's a neat simulation, but the only random mutations the cars can undergo are the ones programmed by humans. The programmer could give them the ability to change gravity, but you could let the simulation run for infinity years and they wouldn't develop the ability on their own, I don't care how many cosmic rays flip how many bits.

An LLM is the same thing as a 2D genetic car, except instead of being programmed to evolve cars that go right, they're programmed to evolve chatbots that produce plausible text. The chatbots that produce less plausible text were outcompeted and died off; the ones remaining are very good at producing plausible text, and that's all they can ever be good at.

So-called "agentic AI" is just the same text generators connected to API calls. The text they're trained on is code that makes API calls, and the LLMs generate code that will plausibly produce similar actions. Instead of spewing text into a chat box, they spew it into a command-line interface. They didn't develop the ability to "do" anything, not by any meaningful definition of agency.

To evolve consciousness, an LLM would have to be programmed to evolve consciousness, and to do that, we would need to know what consciousness is and how to program it.

The only reason the cars can "evolve" is because there are physical principles we understand and can simulate. We know how a wheel works. We understand how gravity affects momentum. We can make a simplified model of the physical world and watch the cars adapt to it.

The only reason an LLM can "evolve" is because we know what plausible text looks like. We have trillions of examples. Language follows rules of grammar and structure that a computer can emulate. Human evaluators can weed out the models that produce less plausible text.

We don't know, in a material sense, what consciousness is. We don't know why we have it. We don't know why some animals have it and others don't. We don't know if it can be quantified. We don't have a model of consciousness or know if one can be created. All we can know about consciousness is what we observe.

Saying it's possible to make an AI conscious is like saying we can make a computer experience the subjective qualia of love. We know what love is, we know the difference between being in love and not being in love. What would it mean to program this feeling into a computer? Is it just making it say "I love you"? No, because we can say "I love you" without being in love. Can a computer learn to actually love? What would that even mean? It's a fun premise for a sci-fi story, but it would be absurd to bring that question into the real world. There's no way to scientifically find an answer. There's nowhere to even start looking for evidence.

Singularitans follow a science-fiction religion that believes, without evidence or even a theory of action, that LLMs will spontaneously mutate and evolve not only consciousness, but God-like super intelligence. They believe this because computers are fast enough and powerful enough to get good at doing tasks that humans program them to do very quickly. Whatever mechanism by which they expect computers to get from A to Z, it's no more grounded in reality than believing God will look down upon a computer from Heaven and, in His infinite compassion, bless it with an eternal soul.

Believing an LLM can become conscious should be just as embarrassing1 as believing a bunch of circles and polygons can learn how to jailbreak their simulation and hack the gravity variable. They're so good at evolving into cars, I know they'll be able to figure out javascript. I swear bro, just give them 5 or 10 years.

  1. But that said, if you were on team "AI is/will be conscious" and you find this post convincing enough to change your mind, I'm not going to make fun of you. We all believe embarrassing things at various points in our lives, and ideally grow out of it. I don't think mocking sincere personal growth is cool or helpful. ↩

sentences.zh: 进化是机器学习的一个有用的比喻，因为进化中的一些概念巧妙地映射到自我改进算法上。

sentences.en: However, this metaphor has become load-bearing for the AI industry, whose existence depends on making sure we confuse the map for the territory forever.
sentences.zh: 然而，这个隐喻已经成为人工智能行业的负担，人工智能行业的存在取决于确保我们永远混淆地图和领土。

sentences.en: If self-improvement algorithms are sort of like evolution, and computers can "evolve" a zillion times faster than organic life, then AI will probably "evolve" into SUPER AI within the next 5 years, or if not, then definitely the next 10, trust me bro.
sentences.zh: 如果自我改进算法有点像进化，并且计算机的“进化”速度比有机生命快无数倍，那么人工智能可能会在未来 5 年内“进化”为超级人工智能，或者如果不是，那么肯定是接下来的 10 年，相信我，兄弟。

blocks.html_en: The problem is that a metaphor is only a metaphor. In reality, machine learning is different from evolution in important ways.

sentences.en: In reality, machine learning is different from evolution in important ways.

blocks.html_en: Have you ever played with the Genetic Algorithm 2D Car Thingy? If not, check it out, it's a fun little toy. Amorphous masses of circles and polygons appear on the left. The circles rotate clockwise. If a circle touches the ground, it will propel the mass of polygons it's attached to forward, until gravity and the shape of the terrain forces it to stop.

sentences.zh: 你玩过遗传算法二维汽车吗？

sentences.zh: 如果没有，请检查一下，这是一个有趣的小玩具。

blocks.html_en: In round 1, most of the masses don't get very far. Maybe one or two will get lucky and be generated with two wheels touching the ground. These will go the farthest, but still quickly fall over because their shape is random, not optimized for traversing the hills and valleys in front of them.

sentences.en: In round 1, most of the masses don't get very far.
sentences.zh: 在第一轮中，大多数群众都没有走得太远。

sentences.en: Maybe one or two will get lucky and be generated with two wheels touching the ground.

sentences.zh: 它们会走得最远，但仍然很快就会翻倒，因为它们的形状是随机的，没有针对穿越前面的山丘和山谷进行优化。

blocks.html_en: Once all the "cars" stop, the universe resets. A new batch of "cars" is generated, using traits from the most successful "cars" in round 1. In this round, the cars that went the furthest reappear with new mutations, and if the mutations make them more car-like, they'll do a little better. This process repeats, and after a few generations, the masses start to resemble cars.

sentences.en: A new batch of "cars" is generated, using traits from the most successful "cars" in round 1.

sentences.en: In this round, the cars that went the furthest reappear with new mutations, and if the mutations make them more car-like, they'll do a little better.

sentences.en: This process repeats, and after a few generations, the masses start to resemble cars.
sentences.zh: 这个过程不断重复，几代人之后，大众开始变得像汽车。

blocks.html_en: Their wheels get more oriented towards the ground; their bodies become longer and sleeker; their weird random appendages shrink and flatten out. Meaningless bundles of shapes were given the same goal we have: to survive as long as possible. And, thanks to a computer simulation, we can watch them evolve to achieve that goal. It's super cool!

sentences.en: Their wheels get more oriented towards the ground; their bodies become longer and sleeker; their weird random appendages shrink and flatten out.
sentences.zh: 他们的轮子变得更加靠近地面；他们的身体变得更长、更光滑；它们奇怪的随机附属物收缩并变平。

sentences.en: Meaningless bundles of shapes were given the same goal we have: to survive as long as possible.

sentences.en: And, thanks to a computer simulation, we can watch them evolve to achieve that goal.

blocks.html_en: Here's a question you might ask: the cars would be able to survive longer if the gravity wasn't so strong, right? But the simulation is stuck at Earth gravity (9.8 m/s) unless the human operator decides to intervene. So why don't the cars learn how to hack the simulation and turn the gravity down? Wouldn't that be a huge evolutionary advantage?

sentences.en: Here's a question you might ask: the cars would be able to survive longer if the gravity wasn't so strong, right?
sentences.zh: 你可能会问一个问题：如果重力不是那么强，汽车就能存活更长时间，对吧？

sentences.zh: 但除非人类操作员决定干预，否则模拟会陷入地球重力 (9.8 m/s)。

sentences.en: So why don't the cars learn how to hack the simulation and turn the gravity down?

sentences.zh: 这难道不是一个巨大的进化优势吗？

blocks.html_en: Well no, you probably wouldn't ask that question, because it's very silly. Obviously the cars aren't literally evolving: it's a metaphor. It's a neat simulation, but the only random mutations the cars can undergo are the ones programmed by humans. The programmer could give them the ability to change gravity, but you could let the simulation run for infinity years and they wouldn't develop the ability on their own, I don't care how many cosmic rays flip how many bits.

blocks.html_en: An LLM is the same thing as a 2D genetic car, except instead of being programmed to evolve cars that go right, they're programmed to evolve chatbots that produce plausible text. The chatbots that produce less plausible text were outcompeted and died off; the ones remaining are very good at producing plausible text, and that's all they can ever be good at.

blocks.html_en: So-called "agentic AI" is just the same text generators connected to API calls. The text they're trained on is code that makes API calls, and the LLMs generate code that will plausibly produce similar actions. Instead of spewing text into a chat box, they spew it into a command-line interface. They didn't develop the ability to "do" anything, not by any meaningful definition of agency.

blocks.html_en: To evolve consciousness, an LLM would have to be programmed to evolve consciousness, and to do that, we would need to know what consciousness is and how to program it.

blocks.html_en: The only reason the cars can "evolve" is because there are physical principles we understand and can simulate. We know how a wheel works. We understand how gravity affects momentum. We can make a simplified model of the physical world and watch the cars adapt to it.

blocks.html_en: Saying it's possible to make an AI conscious is like saying we can make a computer experience the subjective qualia of love. We know what love is, we know the difference between being in love and not being in love. What would it mean to program this feeling into a computer? Is it just making it say "I love you"? No, because we can say "I love you" without being in love. Can a computer learn to actually love? What would that even mean? It's a fun premise for a sci-fi story, but it would be absurd to bring that question into the real world. There's no way to scientifically find an answer. There's nowhere to even start looking for evidence.

blocks.html_en: Singularitans follow a science-fiction religion that believes, without evidence or even a theory of action, that LLMs will spontaneously mutate and evolve not only consciousness, but God-like super intelligence. They believe this because computers are fast enough and powerful enough to get good at doing tasks that humans program them to do very quickly. Whatever mechanism by which they expect computers to get from A to Z, it's no more grounded in reality than believing God will look down upon a computer from Heaven and, in His infinite compassion, bless it with an eternal soul.

content_html_zh:
20 世纪末，有一只名叫 Koko 的大猩猩，因表现出明显的用手语与人类交谈的能力而引起轰动。 正如我们所知，这会对生活产生令人震惊的影响，但科学确定她所做的实际上并不是“使用语言”。 通过强化学习，她开始意识到模仿人类处理者的手势会导致某些结果。 她知道，做出“食物”的手势可能会说服人类给她食物，但她的大脑结构无法让她理解手势以抽象的方式代表食物。 她可以学习单词关联，但她无法理解交流所需的语法和句法，使其真正成为一种“语言”。 我们没有发现智人大猩猩。

这并不是说这是不可能的；而是说这是不可能的。任何使人类大脑发展出语言的突变都可能再次发生，如果真的发生，我们应该认真对待。 我不认为这会像科科那样发生。我们可能会注意到动物以稍微复杂的方式进行交流，但可能需要亿万年的时间才能将这种交流变成我们所认可的语言。 或者我们会发现一种迄今为止未知的动物物种已经经历了这种转变。 极不可能，但它有可能发生。

那么相反呢？ 如果有意识的动物不能自发地学习使用语言，那么使用语言的生物能发展出意识吗？ 有些人认为这是可能的；有些人声称相信这已经发生了，目前现有的法学硕士已经有意识了。 这是我比较怀疑的一种可能性。

首先，我对法学硕士“使用语言”的观点提出质疑。 对于不经意的观察者来说，他们正在做的事情看起来很像使用语言；但为了避免我们忘记，科科也是如此。 法学硕士学习语言的方式基本上是Koko“学习”“语言”方式的高速、高度专业化的版本。 我们制作了一个计算机程序来模拟“想要东西”的动物，然后教它以“得到它想要的东西”的方式模仿人类语言。 如果你有一个虚拟的科科，她的大脑是相同的，但工作速度快一万亿倍，她也可能能够达到类似程度的“学习语言”。

Ted Jiang 写了一篇关于人工智能意识的权威揭穿文章，所以我不会重复他的分析，去读吧。 （如果无法加载完整文章，请尝试禁用 javascript。） 但我认为继续进行动物比较将说明为什么“人工智能意识”不仅是不可能的，而且是一个只有在宗教框架中才有意义的概念。

我们不知道意识何时或如何首次出现，但我们确实知道为什么，因为进化的“原因”总是相同的：意识进化是因为它帮助动物生存。 某些有机体突变了一些类似于原型大脑的特征[编辑：这并不完全正确，请参阅 TNSBWM 的评论]，并具有一些原始的意识火花；这（以某种方式）帮助它比周围纯粹基于刺激的动物生存和繁殖更多的数量。 数百万年来，该生物体一直在与生态位中没有这种突变的生物体竞争，并且随着它们不断繁殖，突变体不断变异。 大脑变得更大，火花也随之增长。

这就是自然世界中进化的运作方式：（突变 + 适宜性）*（时间）= [差异]。 特定利基市场中最有用的差异成为主导差异。

进化是机器学习的一个有用的比喻，因为进化中的一些概念巧妙地映射到自我改进算法上。 然而，这个隐喻已经成为人工智能行业的负担，人工智能行业的存在取决于确保我们永远混淆地图和领土。 如果自我改进算法有点像进化，并且计算机的“进化”速度比有机生命快无数倍，那么人工智能可能会在未来 5 年内“进化”为超级人工智能，或者如果不是，那么肯定是接下来的 10 年，相信我，兄弟。

问题是隐喻只是隐喻。 事实上，机器学习在很多重要方面不同于进化。

你玩过遗传算法二维汽车吗？ 如果没有，请检查一下，这是一个有趣的小玩具。 圆形和多边形的非晶质块出现在左侧。 圆圈顺时针旋转。 如果一个圆接触地面，它将推动其所附着的大量多边形向前移动，直到重力和地形形状迫使其停止。

在第一轮中，大多数群众都没有走得太远。 也许一两个会很幸运，并生成两个轮子接触地面。 它们会走得最远，但仍然很快就会翻倒，因为它们的形状是随机的，没有针对穿越前面的山丘和山谷进行优化。

一旦所有“汽车”停下来，宇宙就会重置。 使用第一轮中最成功的“汽车”的特征生成一批新的“汽车”。 在这一轮中，跑得最远的汽车带着新的突变重新出现，如果这些突变使它们更像汽车，它们就会做得更好一些。 这个过程不断重复，几代人之后，大众开始变得像汽车。

他们的轮子变得更加靠近地面；他们的身体变得更长、更光滑；它们奇怪的随机附属物收缩并变平。 无意义的形状束被赋予了与我们相同的目标：尽可能长时间地生存。 而且，借助计算机模拟，我们可以观察它们的演变以实现这一目标。 太酷了！

你可能会问一个问题：如果重力不是那么强，汽车就能存活更长时间，对吧？ 但除非人类操作员决定干预，否则模拟会陷入地球重力 (9.8 m/s)。 那么为什么汽车不学习如何破解模拟并降低重力呢？ 这难道不是一个巨大的进化优势吗？

嗯，不，你可能不会问这个问题，因为这很愚蠢。 显然，汽车并不是真正意义上的进化：它只是一个隐喻。 这是一个简洁的模拟，但汽车可以经历的唯一随机突变是由人类编程的。 程序员可以赋予他们改变重力的能力，但你可以让模拟运行无限年，他们不会自己开发这种能力，我不在乎有多少宇宙射线翻转多少位。

法学硕士与 2D 基因汽车是一样的，只不过它们不是被编程来进化出正确行驶的汽车，而是被编程为进化出能够产生可信文本的聊天机器人。 产生不太可信文本的聊天机器人在竞争中被击败并消亡。剩下的人非常擅长生成可信的文本，而这就是他们所擅长的。

所谓的“代理人工智能”只是连接到 API 调用的相同文本生成器。 他们接受训练的文本是进行 API 调用的代码，法学硕士生成的代码可能会产生类似的操作。 他们没有将文本喷入聊天框，而是将其喷入命令行界面。 他们没有发展出“做”任何事情的能力，这不是任何有意义的代理定义。

为了进化意识，法学硕士必须被编程来进化意识，要做到这一点，我们需要知道意识是什么以及如何对其进行编程。

汽车能够“进化”的唯一原因是因为有我们理解并可以模拟的物理原理。 我们知道轮子是如何工作的。 我们了解重力如何影响动量。 我们可以制作一个物理世界的简化模型，并观察汽车适应它。

法学硕士能够“发展”的唯一原因是我们知道合理的文本是什么样的。 我们有数万亿个例子。 语言遵循计算机可以模拟的语法和结构规则。 人类评估者可以剔除产生不太可信文本的模型。

从物质意义上来说，我们不知道意识是什么。 我们不知道为什么我们有它。 我们不知道为什么有些动物有它而另一些动物没有。 我们不知道是否可以量化。 我们没有意识模型，也不知道是否可以创建一个。 我们所能知道的关于意识的一切就是我们所观察到的。

说人工智能有意识是可能的，就像说我们可以让计算机体验爱的主观品质一样。 我们知道爱是什么，我们知道恋爱和不恋爱之间的区别。 将这种感觉编入计算机意味着什么？ 难道只是为了表达“我爱你”吗？ 不，因为我们可以在不相爱的情况下说“我爱你”。 计算机能学会真正去爱吗？ 这意味着什么？ 对于科幻故事来说，这是一个有趣的前提，但将这个问题带入现实世界是荒谬的。 没有办法科学地找到答案。 甚至无处开始寻找证据。

奇点主义者遵循一种科幻小说的宗教信仰，他们相信，在没有证据甚至行动理论的情况下，法学硕士不仅会自发地变异和进化意识，还会自发地变异和进化出上帝般的超级智能。 他们相信这一点，因为计算机足够快、足够强大，能够擅长完成人类编程让它们快速完成的任务。 无论他们期望计算机通过什么机制从头到尾，这都与现实无关，就像相信上帝会从天堂俯视一台计算机，并以他无限的同情心祝福它拥有永恒的灵魂一样。

相信法学硕士可以变得有意识，就像相信一堆圆形和多边形可以学习如何越狱他们的模拟并破解重力变量一样令人尴尬。 他们非常擅长进化成汽车，我知道他们能够理解 JavaScript。 我发誓兄弟，只给他们5年或10年的时间。

  1. 但话虽如此，如果你在“人工智能是/将会有意识”的团队中，并且你发现这篇文章足以令人信服地改变你的想法，我不会取笑你。 我们都相信在生活中的不同阶段会遇到令人尴尬的事情，并且最好能从中摆脱出来。 我不认为嘲笑真诚的个人成长是很酷或有帮助的。 ↩
